explanation: Retrospective, context-free per-BPE-token lookup at layer 0: the pole's strength is a fixed function of the single current token, so the same token gives the same value in every context, language and position (a sweep of all 50,254 token ids reproduces every scan value, and input attribution puts 100% of the peak on that token and 0% on the previous one), and a text fires iff at least one of its tokens after the first is in the pole's fixed active set. 'above' dominates that set: bare 'above' 1.11 x max (the value seen inside brackets), ' above' 1.02, ' Above' 0.62, and the word's sense is irrelevant - physical height ('The chart above is wrong.' 1.02) and document back-reference ('the tools above' 1.02) fire identically; 'ABOVE' cannot fire whole because the tokenizer splits it into ' AB'+'OVE' (0.31). The rest of the set is a fixed, semantically heterogeneous slice of about 1,900 of the 50,254 BPE tokens (3.8% of the vocabulary, 1.7% of running prose) that has to be named as tokens rather than as a class, because near-synonyms split badly.
